chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn 'Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Sindi, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no constriction nor expansion except that Allah has in it a favor and a trial.

key_terms.بَسْط: Expansion, ease, or abundance (in provision, health, or circumstances)
key_terms.قَبْض: Constriction, difficulty, or restriction (in provision, health, or circumstances)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of qabd and bast in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that every state of 'constriction' (qabd) or 'expansion' (bast) serves a dual purpose: it is both a divine favor (man) and a trial (ibtala'). This underscores the Shia theological perspective that material and spiritual conditions are not merely circumstantial but are intentional mechanisms for spiritual refinement and testing.
